1.title: Security Testing
1.text: Welcome to Module seventeen: Security Testing. It covers the exam area five. Security Operations and Incident Response. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. five point five Understand security testing: Security readiness testing (for example blue teaming, purple teaming, red teaming). Application testing (for example vulnerability scanning, static analysis, dynamic analysis, threat modeling). Physical penetration testing (for example phishing, tailgating, impersonation). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: five. Security Operations and Incident Response (seventeen point three percent). Exam format: an adaptive exam of one hundred to one hundred twenty-five questions in two hours; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official I S C two C C exam outline.

1.title: Why test security
1.text: Why test security. Security testing finds weaknesses before attackers do and proves that controls work. Every test needs written authorization and clear rules of engagement: scope, timing, methods allowed and contacts. Testing without permission is a crime. Exam tip: Get written permission first. Scope and rules of engagement protect both the tester and the organization.

1.title: Vulnerability scanning and penetration testing
1.text: Vulnerability scanning and penetration testing. The figure shows this: Vulnerability scans find weaknesses; penetration tests try to exploit them.

1.title: Vulnerability scanning and penetration testing, continued
1.text: Vulnerability scanning and penetration testing. Vulnerability scan. Aim: Find and list known weaknesses. How: Automated tool; broad, fast, low risk. Penetration test. Aim: Prove what an attacker could actually do. How: Skilled people exploit weaknesses; deeper and riskier. Authenticated (credentialed). Scanner logs in; more accurate. Unauthenticated. Sees the system like an outsider. Vulnerabilities are scored by severity (for example with C V S S) and handled by risk: fix, mitigate, accept. Scan regularly and after changes. Black box. Tester has no inside information. Gray box. Partial information. White box. Full information (diagrams, code). Exam tip: A scan finds weaknesses; a penetration test exploits them. A scan does not prove an attack would work.

1.title: Security readiness testing: red, blue and purple teams
1.text: Security readiness testing: red, blue and purple teams. Red team. Plays the attacker to test detection and response. Blue team. Defends: monitors, detects, responds. Purple team. Red and blue work together, sharing findings at once to improve defenses. Red team exercises test people, process and technology together, often without warning the defenders (with senior approval). Purple teaming is collaborative and fast learning.

1.title: Application testing
1.text: Application testing. Static analysis (S A S T). What it does: Reads the source code without running it. When: Early, during coding. Dynamic analysis (D A S T). What it does: Tests the running application from outside. When: Test or staging. Vulnerability scanning of dependencies. What it does: Checks libraries for known flaws. When: Continuous. Threat modeling. What it does: Thinks like an attacker at design time: what can go wrong? When: Design phase. Threat modeling often uses stride (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege). Fixing a flaw is cheapest at design time. Exam tip: Static equals code at rest. Dynamic equals program running. Threat modeling happens before the code is written.

1.title: Physical penetration testing
1.text: Physical penetration testing. Physical penetration testing checks building and people controls with authorized attempts to get in or get information. Tailgating. Following an employee through a secured door. Impersonation. Posing as a delivery person, repair technician or manager. Phishing. Fake emails (and calls) to trick staff. Lock picking, badge cloning. Defeating door controls. Dumpster diving. Searching trash for secrets. The tester carries a signed authorization letter (the "get out of jail free" letter) in case of being stopped. Results lead to better locks, badge rules, guard training and awareness.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A team runs an automated tool that lists known weaknesses on all servers. What is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A vulnerability scan. An automated search for known weaknesses is a vulnerability scan.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which test tries to exploit weaknesses to show what an attacker could really do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A penetration test by skilled testers. A penetration test exploits weaknesses to prove real impact.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. In a security exercise the attackers and the defenders share what they learn immediately so that defenses improve quickly. Which team approach is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Purple team, which combines both teams. A purple team combines red and blue teams to share findings at once.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Developers want to find flaws by analyzing the source code before the program is run. Which method is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Static analysis of the source code. Static analysis examines the code without running it.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. The team asks what could go wrong with a new system while it is still being designed. Which activity is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Threat modeling at design time. Thinking like an attacker at design time is threat modeling.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A tester wearing a delivery uniform follows an employee through a secured door. Which two tactics are used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Impersonation and tailgating. Posing as a delivery person is impersonation and following through the door is tailgating.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What must be obtained before any security test? Answer: Written authorization with rules of engagement. Question two. What is the difference between a scan and a penetration test? Answer: A scan lists weaknesses; a penetration test exploits them. Question three. What does the red team do? Answer: Plays the attacker.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is S A S T? Answer: Static analysis of source code. Question five. What does stride support? Answer: Threat modeling. Question six. What is a gray box test? Answer: A test with partial information.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Rules: written authorization, scope, rules of engagement. Scan versus pen test: scan finds known weaknesses; pen test exploits them. Teams: red attacks, blue defends, purple works together. Application: static (code), dynamic (running), dependencies, threat modeling (design, stride). Physical: tailgating, impersonation, phishing, badge cloning; signed letter.
